correctness.rationale: For either agent, bounded-morphism back onto a universal target relation makes every source equivalence class surject onto all m target states, so each class has at least m points. Two-agent properness makes intersections of the two equivalence partitions singleton-or-empty. One class of the first partition therefore meets at least m distinct classes of the second, each with at least m points, giving the m-squared lower bound. The published X-times-X construction supplies equality and preserves S5.

value.rationale: Properization is a recurring semantic step in translations from relational epistemic models to simplicial models. The recent source incurs a quadratic finite-state blow-up, and a later application visibly proliferates worlds. The theorem proves this quadratic cost is an exact worst-case barrier already for the universal two-agent S5 family, so the result directly constrains finite-model and completeness constructions based on properization.
